specification.title: A migration that provides no reversal is reverted
steps: Runner A applies { m1 }. m1 inserts marker m1 and provides no reversal.
Revert with the framework's default selection.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the revert has returned and the reapply has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If a revert reports a migration as reverted, its history entry is absent and its marker is absent.

If a migration provides no reversal, a revert does not report it as reverted while its marker remains: it refuses before changing history, or follows a documented irreversible-migration contract that keeps history and database consistent.

execution.description: Lucid's defaults, with the managed transaction API db.transaction(callback).
execution.form: MigrationRunner.run() on a standalone Database. The migration file is generated for the case.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The caller of revert learns only what the operation reports. If that report says the migration was reverted, the caller treats its effects as gone.
